findings.conditions: variable-size Comm_Resize; two ranks send to each other; MPI_Send not buffered (synchronous/zero eager limit)
findings.reasoning: Zoltan_Comm_Exchange_Sizes first issues blocking MPI_Send of the message size to every procs_to[i] (line 46) and only afterwards posts the blocking MPI_Recv from procs_from[i] (line 54). Communication plans are typically symmetric (A sends to B and B to A), so every rank sits in MPI_Send waiting for a receive that its peer posts only after its own sends complete. This works only because a 1-int message is sent eagerly; under synchronous-mode semantics (or an MPI without buffering) it is a cyclic wait and the program hangs. Irecv-before-Send, as in comm_invert_map.c, would make it safe.

findings.conditions: low-memory migration, object sent to another part on the same process (start_offset=0, left==right==rank), standard send not buffered
findings.reasoning: In the bucket brigade, step i=0 has left==right==rank; since rank<left is false, message_receive(self) runs before message_send(self). message_receive posts the data Irecv and then does a blocking MPI_Send of the ack to itself (line 1669); the matching MPI_Recv of the ack (line 1682) is only executed afterwards in message_send. A blocking send to self with no posted receive completes only if MPI buffers it; otherwise the process deadlocks on itself.

findings.conditions: COMM_PATTERN=A with distance-1 coloring, more than two processes, varying message timing
findings.reasoning: In asynchronous mode D1ParallelColoring uses MPI_Waitsome (also line 1712) and applies whichever neighbours' colour lists have arrived before colouring the next superstep. Which requests complete in a given Waitsome call depends on timing, so the forbidden-colour sets seen by PickColor differ between runs, giving different colourings, numbers of colours and conflict sets (and hence different recolouring work) for identical input. Output is not reproducible run to run.

findings.conditions: RIB/RCB with Tflops_Special (or par_average/par_median exchanges) and sends not buffered
findings.reasoning: The binary-exchange loop has both partners execute MPI_Send(partner) followed by MPI_Recv(partner) (rib.c:927-928). The same Send-then-Recv symmetric exchange appears in par_average.c:135-136, par_median.c:635-636 and par_tflops_special.c:74-75, 142-143, 209-210. Each partner blocks in MPI_Send until the other posts its receive, which happens only after its own send returns; progress relies entirely on eager buffering of the small messages. Without buffering this is a head-to-head deadlock. MPI_Sendrecv would be safe.

findings.conditions: caller-supplied tag reused by another in-flight message on the same communicator
findings.reasoning: Zoltan_Comm_Invert_Map posts nrecvs MPI_Irecv with MPI_ANY_SOURCE and the caller's tag, and records procs_from from status.MPI_SOURCE; the code comment admits it relies on a unique tag. Any other message with the same tag and communicator that is pending (e.g. from user code or a non-collective-separated exchange using the same tag) can be matched instead, giving a wrong procs_from/lengths_from plan, truncation errors or a later hang in Comm_Do. Within Zoltan the surrounding collectives currently separate uses, so this is a latent rather than certain race.
